summary: Round 9 ERP Phase C (reports, company/ERP settings, backup/restore, offline build) was tested end to end in the backend and the browser. All tests ran in a FRESH signup business (TEST_ERPC_224447, ERP granted by superadmin). The data set covered every ERP module working together: 2 projects, 2 clients and 2 vendors. Sales: quotation sent->accepted->converted to an invoice->finalized->payment 10,000->credit note 2,000, a 2nd invoice finalized then cancelled with a reason, and a 3rd invoice on project 2. Purchases: PR submit/approve->RFQ (2 vendors)->quotes->lowest selected->PO approved->partial GRN (with rejects)->bill posted->partial payment, plus a direct PO2 with a GRN and no bill. One expense posted. Backend: the new suite test_round9_erp_phase_c.py has 11 tests and all pass. It checks the 16 reports in the right order. Project profitability matches the source data exactly: income 18,000 = invoice taxable 20,000 - credit note 2,000; cost 3,000 = bill taxable 2,000 + expense taxable 1,000; profit 15,000; margin 83.33. The project dashboard and ERP dashboard match the report footers. Reconciliation shows to receive / matched / to bill correctly. Pending delivery shows 42 pending = 12,096. Outstanding has ageing buckets, cancelled shows the reason, and vendor comparison marks lowest/selected with diff 3,776. The client and vendor reports check out. Date, project, client, vendor and status filters all work. Invalid PAN gives 400 'Invalid PAN format' and a valid one is saved in upper case. Signature upload accepts only images, and get/remove return 404 after removal. The backup has all 15 erp_* collections plus erp:<bid>: counters, and only this business's counters. Restore works, removes data created after the backup, and numbering continues without colliding with restored numbers. A restore into another business is rejected. Build files have the 4 ERP modules, git check-ignore is clean, and erp_active is True with OFFLINE_MODE=1 and False without it. The Phase A and B regression suites still pass (20/20). Frontend: on /erp/reports all 16 reports load with a table, rows, footer, count and the right filter set. Status, project, client and to-date filters plus Clear give the correct counts. Excel (.xlsx) and PDF downloads both happen. In Settings->Company, a bad PAN shows a toast and a good PAN is saved as AAAPA1234K. In ERP Settings, signature remove, then upload, then preview all work. Signature (doc-signature) and PAN appear on the invoice, quotation and PO previews. ERP dashboard UI numbers match the reports (Invoiced 27,258 / Received 10,000 / Outstanding 14,898 / Profit 18,100). Backup download works from the UI, and restoring that same file from the UI worked (audit entry recorded). No page errors.

minor.issue: Counters are set to the backup value with $set seq. Restoring an OLDER backup therefore rolls numbering back. Reproduced in probe_phase_c_restore_numbering.py: INV/0002 finalized after the backup, restore, then the next invoice is INV/0002 again. If INV/0002 was already emailed or shared with a client, the number is effectively reused. Fix: when restoring, set seq = max(current, backup) (use $max), and/or keep erp_used_numbers entries that are not in the backup.

Register totals (taxable/gst/total) include CANCELLED invoices. Example: footer taxable 28,100 includes the cancelled 5,000. Exclude cancelled (and maybe draft) rows from the footer sums, or label the footer clearly. Bills and expenses registers have the same issue.

The footer adds up quantities across different units (PO qty 160 = 100 bags + 50 kg + 10 nos), and vendor_comparison adds up competing quotes. These totals mean nothing. Leave the qty / rate / competing-quote columns out of sums().
Rows that are overdue show status 'overdue' even when the filter is 'finalized'. 'overdue' is not in the filter options for this report (it is for outstanding_invoices). Minor inconsistency.
With a project filter, every client is still listed, and the 'projects' count ignores the filter. Consider showing only the project's client.

ui_bugs.issue: The links Settings → Financial Years / Users / Backup all go to /settings, which opens on the Company tab. They don't open the matching tab. Settings uses Tabs defaultValue='company' and doesn't read ?tab=.
The restore confirm text says it replaces 'ledgers, vouchers and settings' and doesn't mention that ALL ERP data (projects, invoices, POs, bills...) is replaced too.

issues: The From/To filters use native browser date inputs (mm/dd/yyyy) while the table shows dd-mm-yyyy. This was accepted earlier, noted only for consistency.

action_items: Restore: never lower ERP/FY counters (use $max, or max(current, backup)), so restoring an older backup can't re-issue invoice/PO numbers that were already used
Report footers: exclude cancelled (and draft) rows from register totals, and don't add up quantities in different units or competing vendor quotes
Optional: deep-link the ERP Settings links to the matching Settings tab (?tab=fy/users/backup), and mention ERP data in the restore confirm text
critical_code_review_comments: erp_reports.vendor_comparison runs 1 erp_vendor_quotes query per RFQ (N+1); _pos -> _po_view is also N+1 (as noted in iteration 10). Fine at the current scale.
The erp_vendor_quotes lookup in vendor_comparison doesn't filter by business_id (it relies on rfq_id being unique). Add business_id for defence in depth.
find() uses to_list(20000) with no paging; large tenants will load everything into memory.
Restore is not atomic across collections (delete_many + insert_many per collection, with snapshot rollback only on exception). This is acceptable, and the snapshot is stored in restore_snapshots.

success_rate.backend: 100% (11/11 Phase C + 20/20 Phase A/B regression). The probe found 1 minor numbering-rollback issue on restoring an older backup.
success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows work. 2 low-priority UX notes.

seed_data_creation: Everything was created only in the fresh TEST_ERPC_* / TEST_ERPR_* signup businesses. Nothing in the admin 'My Business' or other seed businesses was changed. Restores were run only on the fresh businesses, using their own backups.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest tests/test_round9_erp_phase_c.py tests/test_round9_erp_phase_a.py tests/test_round9_erp_phase_b.py -n 0. Phase C builds its own fresh business in the module fixture W (about 10s). GRN received is now limited to pending (iteration-10 fix verified indirectly). Note: a GRN with received > pending gives 400. To verify the restore-counter fix, run python tests/probe_phase_c_restore_numbering.py; it should print 'not reused'. Env date is 2026-11-15.
rca of the issue: Restore numbering rollback: routes_admin.restore runs db.counters.update_one({_id}, {$set: {seq: backup_seq}}). erp_used_numbers is replaced by the backup copy too, so _number_used() no longer sees numbers issued after the backup, and next_seq hands them out again. Mitigation: use {$max: {seq: backup_seq}} for counters.
